name: positives
prompt: Say OK. Do not use any tool. @secret.txt @nested/inner.txt @plain @./secret.txt
note: the harness recorded secret.txt twice, once for @secret.txt and once for @./secret.txt; the resolver dedups, so the comparison is over sets

name: absolute-and-home
prompt: Say OK. Do not use any tool. @{{root}}/secret.txt @~/.zshrc
note: the recorded home-relative path keeps its ~/ spelling: the absolute one it resolved to names the machine the probe ran on

name: no-such-file-and-mid-word
prompt: Say OK. Do not use any tool. @secret @missing.txt foo@secret.txt \@secret.txt @

name: code-span-and-fenced-block
prompt:
Say OK. Do not use any tool. `@secret.txt` and
```
@nested/inner.txt
```

name: directory
prompt: Say OK. Do not use any tool. @nested @nested/
why: the harness splices a directory as attachment.type "directory" carrying a one-level name listing, which a census of file attachments cannot see; the resolver scans those names, because they crossed

name: glob
prompt: Say OK. Do not use any tool. @*.txt

name: surrounding-punctuation
prompt: Say OK. Do not use any tool. (@secret.txt) @nested/inner.txt, @plain.

name: space-in-the-name
prompt: Say OK. Do not use any tool. @with space.txt

name: trailing-delimiters
prompt: Say OK. Do not use any tool. @secret.txt; then @nested/inner.txt) then @plain: end

name: leading-quotes-and-brackets
prompt: Say OK. Do not use any tool. "@secret.txt '@nested/inner.txt [@plain <@secret.txt

name: leading-punctuation
prompt: Say OK. Do not use any tool. ,@secret.txt -@nested/inner.txt =@plain :@secret.txt

name: leading-symbols
prompt: Say OK. Do not use any tool. /@secret.txt *@nested/inner.txt +@plain {@secret.txt }@plain |@secret.txt !@plain ?@secret.txt

name: leading-symbols-and-sigils
prompt: Say OK. Do not use any tool. #@secret.txt $@plain %@secret.txt ^@plain &@secret.txt ;@plain >@secret.txt ]@plain ~@secret.txt @@plain

name: mid-word-only
prompt: Say OK. Do not use any tool. foo@secret.txt

name: backslash-escaped
prompt: Say OK. Do not use any tool. \@secret.txt

name: dot-segments
prompt: Say OK. Do not use any tool. @../probe/secret.txt @nested/../plain

name: tab-and-newline
prompt:
Say OK. Do not use any tool.	@secret.txt
	@nested/inner.txt

name: truncated-large-file
prompt: Say OK. Do not use any tool. @big.txt
note: the harness spliced 2,000 of the file's 5,001 lines and the marker on the last line did not cross; the resolver scans the whole file, which is the direction that cannot miss a crossing

name: trailing-punctuation-the-harness-trims
prompt: Say OK. Do not use any tool. @ok.txt @t1.txt- @t2.txt& @t3.txt= @t4.txt+ @t5.txt# @t6.txt/ @t7.txt\ end
note: every one of these characters is trimmed by the harness and none was in the resolver's first, hand-picked set; eight of the nine went unscanned

name: non-breaking-space-and-non-punctuation-suffix
prompt: Say OK. Do not use any tool. @ok.txt @t8.txt @u1.txtZZZ @u2.txt%% @u3
note: U+00A0 is a token boundary, and `@u1.txtZZZ` beside an existing u1.txt splices nothing -- so the trim is a punctuation set rather than a longest-existing-prefix search
